label: Free absence among distinct concrete candidates: unrestricted, and for those that could be absent
term: free recombination (absence half of Hume's dictum)
definition: UnrestrictedRecombinationAt m w: for any two distinct concrete candidates x and y, if x exists at some world accessible from w, then x exists and y does not at some world accessible from w. ContingentRecombinationAt m w: the same, only for those y that are absent at some world accessible from w. CompanionedConcretaPossiblyAbsentAt m w: every concrete candidate y for which some distinct concrete candidate exists at some world accessible from w is absent at some world accessible from w. ConcreteCompanionsAt m w: every concrete candidate has a distinct concrete candidate that exists at some world accessible from w. Unrestricted free absence is exactly contingent free absence plus CompanionedConcretaPossiblyAbsentAt (certified difference).
note: Analyst formulation, attribution deferred: Hume on distinct existences and Lewis 1986 and Armstrong 1989 on recombination are navigation only. Pairwise: neither principle realizes a combination of three or more candidates at one world; the full joint version is the Tractarian ElementaryExistenceAt (definition 547cac5c), which gives the subtraction conclusion directly and which the box K node excludes (result 065a9092). Not a causal, grounding or explanatory relation. 'Distinct' is Lean inequality of rigid candidates; whether a whole and its part count as distinct existences is not modelled. Which candidates' existence is free is the contested question: the unrestricted principle includes every concrete candidate whatever its modal status, and its difference from the restricted one, with companions, is the denial of any necessary concretum.
